AssetModel.description:
A single asset entry aligned with §2.4 Asset Identification table.

Combines the §2.4 Asset Record fields (asset_id, name, asset_type,
location, security_attributes, damage_scenario) with a DFDContext block
sourced from §2.3.1 and Threat-Agent-specific device_config metadata.

asset_id format follows the §2.4 convention: 'AS-{n}' (e.g. 'AS-1', 'AS-2').
An explicit id_alias field preserves any internal identifiers for audit.

Kept deliberately domain-neutral — fields apply equally to a Smart Door
Lock BLE controller, a medical infusion pump, and a vehicle ECU.

asset_id.description: Unique asset identifier following §2.4 convention: 'AS-{n}', e.g. 'AS-1', 'AS-2'.  This is the join key for the Traceability Matrix linking Asset → Threat → Risk → Requirement.
asset_id.title: Asset Id

asset_type.description: Optional internal classification (not in §2.4 baseline). e.g. 'firmware', 'REST API endpoint', 'BLE peripheral'.
asset_type.title: Asset Type

location.description: Physical or logical location of the asset per §2.4, e.g. 'on-device', 'cloud-hosted', 'edge-gateway', 'internal VLAN'.
location.title: Location

security_attributes.description: CIA-triad security properties required for this asset per §2.4. Used by the Risk Agent's impact scoring (S/F/O/P) in Phase 2.

damage_scenario.description: Human-readable worst-case damage scenario if this asset is compromised, per §2.4.  Used by Risk Agent for impact scoring. e.g. 'Unauthorised physical entry to premises' or 'Incorrect drug dosage causing patient harm'.
damage_scenario.title: Damage Scenario

dfd_context.description: Data-Flow-Diagram context for this asset, sourced from §2.3.1. retrieval.py reads interfaces and trust_zone from here to build FAISS query vectors and select KB sources.

device_config.description: Threat-Agent-specific technical device configuration. Captures *what security mechanisms the asset has* (distinct from security_attributes which captures *what it needs to protect*). e.g. {'auth_mechanism': 'PIN-only', 'encryption': 'none', 'firmware_version': '2.3.1'}.  These are the primary inputs to retrieval.py's FAISS query embedding.
device_config.title: Device Config

AssetModel.title: AssetModel

DFDContext.description:
Data-Flow-Diagram context sourced from Group 1's §2.3.1 output.

Separates DFD-level context (interfaces, trust zone, flows) from the
Asset Identification table (§2.4).  retrieval.py reads this to determine
which KB sources to query and to build the FAISS query vector.

interfaces.description: Communication interfaces of this asset as extracted from the DFD, e.g. ['BLE 5.0', 'UART', 'OTA update channel'].
interfaces.title: Interfaces

trust_zone.description: Trust boundary zone from the DFD, e.g. 'trusted', 'untrusted', 'DMZ', 'external', 'internal'.
trust_zone.title: Trust Zone

data_flows.description: Data flow names that involve this asset as a source or destination, e.g. ['unlock_command', 'ota_update'].
data_flows.title: Data Flows

DFDContext.title: DFDContext

SecurityAttributes.description:
CIA-triad security properties required for this asset per §2.4.

Distinct from device_config (which captures *what mechanisms the asset has*).
These fields capture *which security properties the asset needs to maintain*,
and are used by the Risk Agent's impact scoring (S/F/O/P) in Phase 2.
SecurityAttributes.title: SecurityAttributes

run_id.description: Unique identifier for this Threat Agent invocation.  Auto-generated if not supplied by the orchestrator.  Propagated to every ThreatScenario, log entry, and SCRS write record.
run_id.title: Run Id

use_case_id.description: Optional stable use-case identifier from the orchestrator; derived from the use_case text when absent.
use_case_id.title: Use Case Id

use_case.description: Natural-language description of the system use case being threat-modelled.  Minimum 10 chars to reject trivially empty submissions; the LLM uses this as the top-level context.
use_case.title: Use Case

system_model.description: Serialized system model (DFD/UML description, data flows, trust boundaries) as a string.  Structured formats (JSON/YAML) are accepted; perceive() normalises this into NormalizedInput.
system_model.title: System Model

assets.description: Ordered list of assets within the system model.  Must contain at least one asset; retrieval.py iterates over this list to build FAISS query vectors.
assets.title: Assets

kb_snapshot_version.description: Version or content-hash of the KB snapshot to use.  Logged verbatim for reproducibility (Section 2.7).  Use 'latest' to resolve to the current KB at runtime.
kb_snapshot_version.title: Kb Snapshot Version

requested_at.description: UTC timestamp when the orchestrator submitted this input.
requested_at.title: Requested At
